html:
The Kabi Kabi, also spelt Gubbi Gubbi or Gabi Gabi, are an Aboriginal people of southeast Queensland, in country that covers the present Sunshine Coast and the hinterland around Gympie.

Their neighbours were the Butchulla of K'gari (Fraser Island) to the north, the Gureng Gureng further north and the Barunggam and Wakka Wakka inland. Every few years, when the bunya pines fruited heavily, peoples from across the region gathered in the Bunya Mountains and the Blackall Range for great feasts on the bunya nuts, with ceremonies, trade and marriages.

In the 1840s and 1850s settlers moved onto their land, and during the frontier wars there were several mass killings of Kabi Kabi people. Gold at Gympie from 1867 brought thousands of miners. In 2024 a court recognised Kabi Kabi native title over a large area of the Sunshine Coast. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
sum: The Kabi Kabi, also spelt Gubbi Gubbi or Gabi Gabi, are an Aboriginal people of southeast Queensland, in country that covers the present Sunshine Coast and the hinterland around Gympie.
